# What will your SSH server really do? sshd_config Check

> Paste /etc/ssh/sshd_config and the files in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d: the tool reads them in sshd's order and shows the value that wins for each setting (sshd keeps the first value it reads), lines sshd ignores (a cloud-init drop-in's PasswordAuthentication yes beating your no), drop-ins it never reads (names without .conf), flush-left lines that still belong to a Match block, keywords that stop sshd starting, and PermitRootLogin yes, password logins (also through PAM keyboard-interactive), weak ciphers, MACs and key exchange, StrictModes no, PermitUserEnvironment and forwarding options. Each finding has its file, line and fix. Free, runs in your browser, nothing uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). A static read of the files you give it, not a security audit and not sshd -T; a clean result is not proof a server is safe. The reading follows OpenSSH 9.6p1's servconf.c and the sshd_config(5) manual of that release (Ubuntu 24.04's version), and agrees with that release's real sshd -t and sshd -T -C on 2,000 generated configurations (82,598 checks, including Match all, which overrides earlier settings for every connection rather than returning to global scope); defaults may differ on other releases. Not affiliated with the OpenSSH project.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/sshd-config-check/)
- [sshd_config mistakes explained: ignored lines, unread drop-ins, Match traps and the fix](https://marisstella.app/sshd-config-check/sshd-config-mistakes-explained.html)

## CLI

- `sudo node check.mjs /etc/ssh` reads sshd_config and every file its Include lines match, in order, and prints file:line findings and how people can log in; `./ssh` reads a copy in a repo as if it were /etc/ssh; `--user U --group G --addr A --host H` shows what one connection gets from the Match blocks; `--format json`; `--fail-on-risk` (exit 2 on an error, high or medium). Node 18+, no dependencies.
